items.title: Individual and differential harm in redistricting
items.author: Christopher T. Kenny
items.content: McCartan and Kenny develop a framework for quantifying the individual-level impacts of redistricting in the USA, showing its applicability for identifying partisan gerrymandering and differential effects across populations.

items.title: Fluctuations in arousal reflect latent state transitions that facilitate behavioural optimization
items.author: Matthew R. Nassar
items.content: Li, Marble et al. examine how moment-to-moment fluctuations in arousal optimize behaviour by signalling environmental transitions and facilitate rapid adjustments of mental context.

items.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
items.author: Diyi Yang
items.content: In this mixed-methods study, Zhang et al. examine AI companionship and psychological well-being, finding that the association depends on usage patterns and users’ offline social contexts.

items.title: Longitudinal effect of early social media use on standardized learning outcomes during school career
items.author: Giovanni Vezzoli
items.content: Analysing data from 5,227 students from northern Italy, this article finds causal evidence that early engagement with social media adversely affects learning outcomes.

items.title: Negative influence of early social media use on school outcomes
items.content: A longitudinal study of Italian students revealed a significant negative effect of early use of social media on later academic performance during lower-secondary school years (grades 6 to 8 in Italy, corresponding to ages 11–14 years old) in mathematics and Italian compared with later social media adoption.

items.title: A life-course map of health risks associated with exposure to second-hand smoke
items.content: We synthesized evidence from 111 meta-analyses to map the comprehensive health risks that are associated with second-hand smoke exposure (SHSE) throughout the life course. Our analyses confirm the strong association of SHSE with lung cancer, cardiovascular disease and a range of adverse fetal and child health outcomes. Moreover, we identify research gaps that should be addressed to inform targeted tobacco control.

items.title: Insights from climate psychology for misinformation research
items.author: Matthew J. Hornsey
items.content: Climate change and misinformation are interconnected global crises shaped by tensions between individual, collective and vested interests. Drawing on climate psychology, we distil six insights for misinformation research to strengthen policy relevance, systems thinking and resilience to attacks.

items.title: Association of traumatic experiences with depressive symptoms among LGBTQ+ population in China
items.author: Huan Song
items.content: Yang et al. found that trauma is highly prevalent among LGBTQ+ individuals in China and linked to depression. Unhealthy behaviours, low social support and negative coping partly explain this relationship, highlighting key targets for intervention.
